title: Longest Block With Equally Many a, b and c

concept.title: The key is a pair of differences
body: In a block that has the same number of `a`, `b` and `c`, the three counts are equal, which means `count(b) - count(a) = 0` **and** `count(c) - count(a) = 0`. For prefixes, let `d1 = count_b - count_a` and `d2 = count_c - count_a` (counted from the start of the word). A block between two prefixes is balanced exactly when **both differences are the same at the two ends**.

This is the two-dimensional version of "equally many 0s and 1s". The key is a **pair of numbers**, and the map stores the **first** position of every key. In C++ and Java the pair can be packed into one number.

statement: A word consists only of the letters `a`, `b` and `c`. Find the length of the longest block of consecutive letters that contains the same number of `a`, `b` and `c`. If there is none, print 0.
inputFormat: A single word of the letters a, b and c.

examples.note: The whole word has three of each letter: length 9.

hints: Count a, b and c in every prefix.
A block is balanced when both `count_b - count_a` and `count_c - count_a` are equal at its two ends.
Store the first position of every pair of differences in a map.

explanation: Two prefixes with the same pair `(count_b - count_a, count_c - count_a)` enclose a balanced block; the first position of each pair gives the longest block.
solution.complexity: Time O(n) on average, space O(n).
